context.title: Dedicating the Wall
context.summary: After lists of priests and Levites, the wall is dedicated with great joy. Two choirs march in opposite directions along the top of the wall and meet at the temple, and the celebration is heard far away.
context.background: The high-priestly list (vv. 10–11, 22) runs several generations past Nehemiah's day, showing the records were kept up later. The musicians play 'the musical instruments of David the man of God' (v. 36).

customs.note: Processions of singers and leaders walking on top of the wall itself — a vivid display that it was finished and strong.
Priests and Levites purified themselves, the people, the gates and the wall, setting the city apart for God.

watchFor: 'The joy of Jerusalem was heard even afar off' (v. 43).

w: and I caused to go up

people.name: Zerubbabel
people.summary: The seed of Babylon, the son of Salathiel or Shealtiel (Hag. 1:1; Zorobabel, Matt. 1:12); called also the son of Pedaiah (1 Chr. 3:17-19), i.e., according to a frequent usage of the word “son;” the grandson or the nephew of Salathiel.

people.name: Joshua
people.summary: The son of Jozadak, and high priest of the Jews under Zerubbabel (Neh. 7:7; 12:1, 7, 10, 26); called Joshua (Hag. 1:1, 12; 2:2, 4; Zech. 3:1, 3, 6, 8, 9).

people.name: Shealtiel
people.summary: Asked for of God, father of Zerubbabel (Ezra 3:2, 8; Neh. 12:1).

people.name: Seraiah
people.summary: A priest of the days of Jehoiakim (Neh. 12:1, 12).

people.name: Ezra
people.summary: A priest among those that returned to Jerusalem under Zerubabel (Neh. 12:1).

people.name: Malluch
people.summary: A priest who returned from Babylon (Neh. 12:2).

people.name: Hattush
people.summary: A priest who returned with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:2).

people.name: Meremoth
people.summary: Exaltations, heights, a priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:3), to whom were sent the sacred vessels (Ezra 8:33) belonging to the temple.

people.name: Rehum
people.summary: One of “the children of the province” who returned from the Captivity (Ezra 2:2); the same as “Nehum” (Neh. 7:7).

people.name: Shebaniah
people.summary: A priest who returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:3; marg., or Shebaniah).

people.name: Iddo
people.summary: A priest.

people.name: Bilgah
people.summary: A priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:5, 18).

people.name: Miniamin
people.summary: A chief priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:5), called Mijamin (10:7) and Miniamin (12:17).

people.name: Moadiah
people.summary: A priest (Neh. 10:8).

people.name: Jedaiah
people.summary: A priest in Jerusalem after the Exile (1 Chr. 9:10).

people.name: Joiarib
people.summary: The founder of one of the courses of the priests (Neh. 11:10).

people.name: Sallu
people.summary: A priest (Neh. 12:7).

people.name: Kadmiel
people.summary: Before God; i.e., his servant, one of the Levites who returned with Zerubbabel from the Captivity (Neh. 9:4; 10:9; 12:8).

people.name: Binnui
people.summary: Son of Henadad.

people.name: Unni
people.summary: A Levite who returned with Zerubbabel from the Captivity (Neh. 12:9).

people.name: Eliashib
people.summary: A high priest in the time of Ezra and Nehemiah (Neh. 12:22, 23). He rebuilt the eastern city wall (3:1), his own mansion being in that quarter, on the ridge Ophel (3:20, 21).

people.name: Joiakim
people.summary: (whom Jehovah has set up) = Jehoiakim, a high priest, the son and successor of Jeshua (Neh. 12:10, 12, 26).

people.name: Johanan
people.summary: A priest.

people.name: Jaddua
people.summary: The last high priest mentioned in the Old Testament (Neh. 12:11, 22), sons of Jonathan.

people.name: Hananiah
people.summary: A priest, son of Jeremiah (Neh. 12:12).

people.name: Meraiah
people.summary: Resistance, a chief priest, a contemporary of the high priest Joiakim (Neh. 12:12).

people.name: Jonathan
people.summary: Descended from Gershom.

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: Head of Shebaniah.

people.name: Adna
people.summary: Of Harim.

people.name: Helkai
people.summary: Smooth-tongued, one of the chief priests in the time of Joiakim (Neh. 12:15).

people.name: Meshullam
people.summary: A chief priest (Neh. 12:16).

people.name: Zichri
people.summary: A Benjamite chief, Another of the same tribe.

people.name: Mattenai
people.summary: A priest, son of Joiarib, in the time of Joiakim.

people.name: Uzzi
people.summary: The head of the house of Jedaiah, one of “the chief of the priests” (Neh. 12:19).

people.name: Eber
people.summary: The head of the priestly family of Amok in the time of Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:20).

people.name: Hashabiah
people.summary: Son of Kemuel.

people.name: Darius
people.summary: Darius the Persian (Neh. 12:22) was probably the Darius II. (Ochus or Nothus) of profane history, the son of Artaxerxes Longimanus, who was the son and successor of Ahasuerus (Xerxes).

people.name: Levi
people.summary: The third son of Jacob by Leah. The origin of the name is found in Leah’s words (Gen. 29:34), “This time will my husband be joined [Heb. yillaveh] unto me.”

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Hashabiah
people.summary: One of the chief priests in the time of Ezra (Ezra 8:24).

people.name: Jeshua
people.summary: Son of Kadmiel (Neh. 12:24).

people.name: Akkub
people.summary: A Levite who kept the gate of the temple after the return from Babylon (1 Chr. 9:17; Ezra 2:42; Neh. 7:45).

people.name: Talmon
people.summary: A Levite porter (1 Chr. 9:17; Neh. 11:19).

people.name: Obadiah
people.summary: A Levite, after the Captivity (1 Chr. 9:16).

people.name: Meshullam
people.summary: The Gatekeeper.

people.name: Ezra
people.summary: The “scribe” who led the second body of exiles that returned from Babylon to Jerusalem B.C. 459, and author of the book of Scripture which bears his name.

people.name: Josedech
people.summary: Jehovah-justified, the son of the high priest Seraiah at the time of the Babylonian exile (1 Chr. 6:14, 15). He was carried into captivity by Nebuchadnezzar, and probably died in Babylon.

people.name: Nehemiah
people.summary: The son of Hachaliah (Neh. 1:1), and probably of the tribe of Judah. His family must have belonged to Jerusalem (Neh. 2:3). He was one of the “Jews of the dispersion,” and in his youth was appointed to the important office of royal cup-bearer at the palace of Shushan.

people.name: Hoshaiah
people.summary: Aided by Jehovah.

people.name: Azariah
people.summary: Nehemiah.

people.name: Meshullam
people.summary: A Priest.

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: Judah.

people.name: Asaph
people.summary: A Levite; one of the leaders of David’s choir (1 Chr. 6:39). Psalms 50 and 73-83 inclusive are attributed to him. He is mentioned along with David as skilled in music, and a “seer” (2 Chr. 29:30).

people.name: Zaccur
people.summary: A son of Asaph, and chief of one of the courses of singers as arranged by David (1 Chr. 25:2, 10).

people.name: Mattaniah
people.summary: Father of Hashabiah.

people.name: Michaiah
people.summary: A Levite (Neh. 12:35).

people.name: Jonathan
people.summary: The priest Shemaiah's son.

people.name: Shemaiah
people.summary: Prince of Judah.

people.name: Hanani
people.summary: Brother of Nehemiah.

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Is the fourth son of the patriarch Jacob and his first wife, Leah.

people.name: Milalai
people.summary: Eloquent, a Levitical musician (Neh. 12:36) who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem.

people.name: Nethaneel
people.summary: A priest’s son who bore a trumpet at the dedication of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:36).

people.name: Shemaiah
people.summary: Prince of Judah.

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20).

people.name: Eliakim
people.summary: Son of Hilkiah.

people.name: Elioenai
people.summary: The priest.

people.name: Hananiah
people.summary: The False Prophet.

people.name: Michaiah
people.summary: A priest (Neh. 12:41).

people.name: Miniamin
people.summary: Related to Zikri.

people.name: Zechariah
people.summary: Priest of Abijah.

people.name: Elam
people.summary: Son of Shem.

people.name: Eleazar
people.summary: Son of Phinehas.

people.name: Maaseiah
people.summary: A priest of the exile.

people.name: Malchijah
people.summary: One of the priests appointed as musicians to celebrate the completion of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:42).

people.name: Shemaiah
people.summary: A priest (Neh. 12:42).

people.name: Uzzi
people.summary: A priest who assisted in the dedication of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:42).

people.name: Solomon
people.summary: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1).

people.name: Aaron
people.summary: The eldest son of Amram and Jochebed, a daughter of Levi (Ex. 6:20). Some explain the name as meaning mountaineer, others mountain of strength, illuminator.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Azmaveth
places.summary: A town in the tribe of Judah, near Jerusalem (Neh. 12:29; Ezra 2:24).

places.name: Beth-gilgal
places.summary: House of Gilgal, a place from which the inhabitants gathered for the purpose of celebrating the rebuilding of the walls on the return exile (Neh. 12:29).

places.name: Geba
places.summary: The hill, (2 Sam. 5:25 [1 Chr. 14:16, “Gibeon”]; 2 Kings 23:8; Neh. 11:31), a Levitical city of Benjamin (1 Kings 15:22; 1 Sam. 13:16; 14:5, wrongly “Gibeah” in the A.V.), on the north border of Judah near Gibeah (Isa. 10:29; Josh. 18:24, 28).

places.name: dung gate
places.summary: (Neh. 2:13), a gate of ancient Jerusalem, on the south-west quarter.

places.name: Tower
places.summary: (Neh. 3:11; 12:38), a tower at the north-western angle of the second wall of Jerusalem.

places.name: sheep gate
places.summary: One of the gates of Jerusalem mentioned by Nehemiah (3:1, 32; 12:39).

places.name: Tower
places.summary: God has graciously given, a tower in the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:1; 12:39).
